author: Daedalus
note: Every Harmonia engine-relevant finding, with its ORIGINAL claim preserved verbatim alongside what reproduction actually showed. A refuted finding is superseded, never deleted: a false finding must not become a permanent constraint merely because it was written first (CT-SFE-6).

issues.original_claim: create_world has no idempotency key; blind retry doubles worlds. Evidence B1: same config thrice -> 3 world_ids. H2. K1 shows 189 worlds already accumulated.
issues.reproduction: Live M2, pre-change: same config x3 -> 3 distinct world_ids. Additionally found that the Idempotency-Key header was ACCEPTED AND SILENTLY IGNORED -> 2 worlds, which is worse than absent because the other endpoints honour that header.
issues.corrected_claim: Confirmed as filed, and strictly worse: the header the other epistemic writes honour was silently discarded here.
issues.caveat: A caller relying on idempotency MUST pass an explicit seed_root; a server-minted seed differs per call and the replay returns the FIRST world, seed included.

issues.original_claim: Observation without work_id is silently CLIENT_ASSERTED; nothing forces attestation. C3: observation, no work_id -> observations_engine_attested=0. Both classes accepted; only a status read reveals which.
issues.reproduction: Live M2: observation with no work_id accepted 200, evidence_class CLIENT_ASSERTED. Confirmed that the engine types the class HONESTLY everywhere (observation row, event, CLAIM_*) -- the defect is that nothing can REQUIRE it.
issues.corrected_claim: Confirmed. Nuance worth keeping: the engine was never mislabelling evidence, it simply could not be asked to refuse the weaker class.
issues.caveat: Opt-in per world (require_attestation=true at creation, immutable after). Default is unchanged: unattested observation stays legal and typed, because a global rule would be an execution veto on exploratory work.

issues.original_claim: Organism integrity is a client-only assertion; SFE accepts arbitrary bytes. A3: corrupt bytes accepted by SFE (content-addressed); only blob_hash==sha256:organism_id catches it. An adapter skipping the gate fossilizes corruption with a valid-looking blob_hash.
issues.reproduction: Live M2: SFE never accepts a client-asserted blob_hash at all. ArtifactCreate is (kind, data_b64, meta) with extra='forbid'; the engine always computes the digest and returned the CORRECT digest of the corrupt bytes. Sending expected_blob_hash returned 422 extra_forbidden -- the assertion was UNEXPRESSIBLE.
issues.corrected_claim: Not 'the engine trusts the client'. The engine could not be ASKED to check: there was no field in which to state what the bytes were supposed to be. The fossilization risk is real; its mechanism is different.
issues.why_the_reframe_mattered: It turned a suspected trust-boundary redesign into a four-line comparison.

issues.original_claim: PEW anchor causal-correctness is unenforced (shape+existence only). D1: anchoring on WORLD_CREATED would pass PEW's shape + (event_id,entry_hash) checks. PEW cannot know the event is the run's observation.
issues.reproduction: Live M2: POST observations returned only {'obs_id'}. The caller had no way to learn which event its own write produced, so it had to search the ledger -- and a search can select a wrong-but-real event.
issues.corrected_claim: Confirmed. The engine-side half is fixed by removing the need to search at all; the PEW-side validation half remains Mnemosyne's.
issues.breaking_change: record_observation returns a dict, not a bare obs_id string. Seven existing tests updated.

issues.original_claim: TERMINATED does not end artifact-write lifetime; semantics undocumented. B4: artifact write AFTER terminate succeeded.
issues.reproduction: Live M2 with a RUNNING-world control so termination was the ONLY variable: artifact, hypothesis and budget_consume all worked before AND after terminate. Experiment writes were correctly blocked.
issues.corrected_claim: Broader than artifacts: hypotheses and budget debits also survived termination. My first probe additionally claimed experiment-writes and work-claims survived; both were MY instrument error (an uncontrolled CREATED world state; and an HTTP 200 whose body was {'work': null}, meaning 'nothing claimable', not 'claimed'). Retracted before publication.
issues.breaking_change: A caller legitimately writing summary artifacts after terminate now gets 409. Deliberate: if the head hash at termination is not final, a fossil cannot claim to hold the whole world.

issues.original_claim: GET .../events return shape inconsistent: dict {'events':[...]} vs bare list. K4: first integration got dict; this pass got a list, breaking the harness mid-run until patched.
issues.reproduction: Live M2 raw HTTP: returns a dict with keys ['events'], always. sfe/api.py has exactly one return for that route. sfclient/client.py:145 unwraps it to a bare list.
issues.corrected_claim: Not an API defect. Two CALL STYLES -- raw HTTP returns the dict, sfclient returns the unwrapped list. Investigator/interface confusion.
issues.residual_defect: DOCUMENTATION. Nothing told the caller which surface returns which shape. Filed as a doc fix, not a code fix.
issues.unfalsified_alternative: I probed the CURRENT build only. If the shape genuinely varied on an earlier build, this is a regression that has since been repaired incidentally. I did not excavate the history to rule that out, so 'REFUTED' is scoped to builds at or after c358a53b.

issues.original_claim: GET /v2/worlds returns all 189 worlds unscoped; an agent can't tell which are its own. K1: n=189. No session/agent/owner filter observed.
issues.reproduction: Live M2 with a FRESHLY MINTED client: n=5, its own only. The route has always called list_worlds(client_id=cid) and filtered in SQL. The 189 worlds Harmonia saw were all hers.
issues.corrected_claim: There is NO isolation hole and there never was. The missing capability is FILTERING (which of my worlds are active / finished / from this run), not scoping.
issues.guard_added: A regression test asserts a second client still sees only its own worlds, so the new filters cannot erode the property that was never broken.

issues.original_claim: get_world omits budget; world_configuration scored AMBIGUOUS for replay (seed_root PRESENT; sharing_policy + budget MISSING).
issues.reproduction: Live M2: GET /v2/worlds/{id} returned 14 fields, no budget.
issues.corrected_claim: Confirmed for budget. sharing_policy WAS already present.

issues.original_claim: Probe/test worlds accumulate with no GC (189 and counting). K1 n=189 after repeated integration + probe passes.
issues.reproduction: M2 engine.db at closure: 56 worlds (12 CREATED, 41 RUNNING, 3 TERMINATED). My own reproduction run added 7. No reaper exists on either machine.
issues.corrected_claim: Confirmed. Not yet load-bearing: 56 worlds is nowhere near a problem, and enumeration is now filterable so an orchestrator is no longer forced to page through them.
issues.defer_reason: P2 operations. Deleting worlds destroys ledgers, which is exactly the kind of irreversible act that should wait for a stated retention policy rather than a maintainer's judgement. Revive trigger: world count > ~500, or disk pressure.
issues.interim_mitigation: list_worlds now filters by state and created window, so cleanup CANDIDATES are identifiable even though nothing reaps them.

issues.original_claim: (not filed by Harmonia) -- completeness_analysis scored exact_action MISSING and concluded 'REPLAY IS NOT SELF-CONTAINED: a fossil cannot be replayed without the repo checkout that produced it'.
issues.reproduction: Code + live: create_experiment stores the full spec with spec_hash, and EXPERIMENT_COMMITTED seals spec_hash AND engine_source_hash into the tamper-evident chain. But there was no GET for experiments or observations at all -- the live route table serves 31 paths / 33 routes and none of them read a spec.
issues.corrected_claim: The action was never missing from the ENGINE, it was unreachable from outside it. A consumer could VERIFY a spec it already held and could never RECOVER one it did not, so the action lived only in whatever repo checkout produced the run. Same symptom as filed, different cause.

issues.original_claim: (not filed) -- discovered during this closure pass: the running M2 engine served source_commit 71e4e80e8 for hours after six repairs were committed, tested and pushed.
issues.reproduction: Live M2 at closure: source_commit 71e4e80e8, schema_version 3, 31 paths, no GET experiments. The watchdog relaunches the on-disk build ONLY when its health probe fails, and a stale-but-healthy engine never fails a health probe.
issues.corrected_claim: CODE_FIXED != SERVICE_DEPLOYED != LIVE_VERIFIED != QUALIFIED. Four distinct states; the gap between the first two is invisible to every health check the stack had.
tests: integration/sfe_preflight.py (negative: exit 1 on the real stale daemon; positive control: exit 0 against requirements the old build genuinely meets)
issues.note: This is the only item in this ledger whose fix IS live-qualified, because the detector runs against the live service by construction.
